summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.3% YoY to INR51.4 crores, but adjusted EBITDA fell 14.5% to INR8.1 crores as growth investments were front-loaded into H1.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 14.3% YoY to INR51.4 crores, with Uniware up 12.8% and Shipway up 16.8%. Adjusted EBITDA declined 14.5% YoY to INR8.1 crores on planned investments in AI-led product, talent and sales and marketing. PAT rose 20.2% to INR4.7 crores, helped by tax benefits recognised in the quarter. Management guided that investments are front-loaded into H1 FY27, with profitability improvement from H2 FY27, Uniware growth above 15% and Shipway growth above 20% from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Uniware (OMS/WMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 12.8% YoY; stand-alone adjusted EBITDA rose to INR11 crores from INR9.1 crores. Added 115 enterprise customers (vs 88 a year ago, +30.7%). Growth ex-exited top-10 client was above 15%.

segments.name: Shipway (courier aggregation)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 16.8% YoY. Management is raising investment after running near breakeven in part of FY26, targeting 20%+ growth from Q4 FY27 and breakeven in Q3 FY27. Management estimates a INR4,000 crore addressable market where it holds a single-digit share.

segments.name: ConvertWay
segments.commentary: Described as performing steadily; product being extended to wider use cases and larger enterprises. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Uniware growth expected to exceed 15% from Q4 FY27 onwards, as Q4 FY27 is the first like-for-like quarter after the top-10 client exit in Q3 FY26.
Shipway growth expected to reach 20%+ YoY from Q4 FY27; Shipway to operate below adjusted EBITDA breakeven in H1 FY27 and at breakeven from Q3 FY27.
Investment front-loaded in H1 FY27 and expected to continue through the current quarter; profitability improvement expected from H2 FY27. Investment amount described only as 'a few crores'.
Uniware adjusted EBITDA margin expected to stay in a similar ballpark to the ~40% level of last year (management cited a move from 32% to 35% on run-rate basis).
Long-term aspiration for Uniware growth to move to late teens and beyond 20%.
capex_capacity: No capex figures or capacity disclosures were given. An analyst noted capex under INR20 crores over two years; management did not dispute this.
Growth investments focused on three areas: AI-led product development (agentic systems), talent and capability additions, and sales and marketing capacity expansion.
Management has launched three modules over the last 12-18 months (UniCapture, UniReco, UniBot) and cited upcoming AI-led launches.
Checkout product being evaluated; launch timing not given.
demand_pricing: Enterprise customer additions: 115 in Q1 FY27 vs 88 a year ago; Q4 FY26 had nearly 149. Management says acquisition is 30-50% above the listing-time run rate of 85-90 per quarter.
Marquee adds in the quarter: Amul, Haldiram's, STUDDS, Pigeon, Mahindra Logistics, The Sleep Company, Snoonu and Namshi (international). Opptra onboarded as a customer for SE Asia and D2C operations.
Module adoption: 40-45% of Uniware enterprise customers use quick commerce and B2B modules; 6-7% use UniReco; 3-4% use UniCapture within two quarters of launch.
Uniware enterprise base is 1,100+ customers. Average realisation is about INR1 lakh per month, broadly stable.
Management said NRR has been 100%+ for several years and expects it to stay there in FY27, but did not give a current quarter figure. Logo churn is mainly small brands shutting down.
Shipway-Uniware customer overlap is 10%+ and has been stable for a couple of quarters while absolute overlap grows.
On competition, management says it is the premium market leader in Uniware and sees a large opportunity against the market leader in courier aggregation.

qa_highlights.question: When will Shipway synergies and acquisition amortisation be absorbed, and when will EBITDA margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investments are front-loaded in H1, with results visible in H2 FY27 and growth improving from Q4 FY27. No quantified margin or amortisation timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ESOP expense so high, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOPs are amortised over four years from grant. About INR2.5 crores was booked this quarter, and the quarterly run-rate is expected at INR2.5-4 crores over the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Shipway revenue been flat near INR20 crores, and when does it ramp up and reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 15%+ growth for two quarters, targeting 20%+ from Q4 FY27 and breakeven in Q3 FY27. Shipway is to be run at breakeven, reinvesting profits.

qa_highlights.question: Why do large clients prefer the market-leading aggregator over Shipway, and how many Uniware top-10 clients use Shipway?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the competitor is the aggregation leader and some overlap is natural. Shipway-Uniware overlap is 10%+ and rising in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI-enabled self-built software (vibe coding) displace Uniware?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that Uniware's relationships with ecosystem players, switching costs, maintenance needs and audit-grade data make it resilient; it sees AI as strengthening the system of record.

qa_highlights.question: What are the steady-state margin targets for Uniware and Shipway?
qa_highlights.answer: Uniware adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to stay near last year's ~40% level. Shipway is to operate at breakeven, with profits reinvested for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an M&A pipeline, and is a fund raise planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating start-ups in exploratory stage, with criteria of existing-customer fit, good product and team, reasonable valuation, and profitability or a path to it. No fund raise is planned because cash is building.

risks_watch: Shipway growth must step up from ~15%+ to 20%+ YoY from Q4 FY27 and reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q3 FY27; H1 FY27 is expected to be below breakeven.
Uniware growth must reach 15%+ from Q4 FY27 as the top-10 client exit laps; Q1 FY27 growth was 12.8% reported.

Adjusted EBITDA is down 14.5% YoY and reported EBITDA is pressured by ESOP expense (~INR2.5 crores this quarter, guided INR2.5-4 crores per quarter over the next year); watch whether H2 FY27 profitability improves as guided.
Investment quantum was described only as 'a few crores' with no annualised figure; the timing of H2 profitability recovery and growth-driven payback is unquantified.
Q1 PAT growth was helped by tax benefits, so underlying earnings growth is weaker than the reported 20.2%.
Shipway-Uniware overlap stuck at 10%+ and a competitor aggregator is listing; watch whether large Uniware clients begin adopting Shipway in absolute numbers.
key_quotes: These investments will be funded through a portion of the earnings we generate while we continuing to add cash to our balance sheet.

Most of these investments will be front-loaded in H1 FY '27 with benefits expected to build through growth and operating leverage, leading to an improving profitability trajectory in H2 FY '27 and beyond.
It will be hard for us to tell the number right now, but it is -- for the last many years, has maintained 100% plus, and we're confident that it will maintain 100% plus even for this year as well.

The investment in terms of absolute is in the range of a few crores and will continue for the current quarter, post which we anticipate some of these investments to start demonstrating results and show improvement in our growth percentage as well.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term growth outlook and on Uniware's stickiness, but cautious and often vague on quantification: it gave no investment amount beyond 'a few crores', no current-quarter NRR, and no M&A target details. Several answers deflected or reframed questions, and the CEO noted he was unwell during the call.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 14.3% YoY to INR51.4 crore, with Uniware guided to 15%+ and Shipway to 20%+ growth from Q4 FY27, backed by 115 enterprise adds (+30.7% YoY); no physical capacity or capex was disclosed, and H1 investment is front-loaded so profitability lags.
